AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Hematoma evacuation is regular treatment for acute traumatic epidural hematoma (ATEDH) patients meeting with surgery indications. However, it is an invasive approach performed under general anesthesia. Here, a novel minimally invasive method of endovascular embolization with subsequent drainage surgery and use of urokinase was established to treat ATEDH under local anesthesia.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: a novel minimally invasive method of endovascular embolization with subsequent drainage surgery and use of urokinase was established to treat ATEDH under local anesthesia. Firstly, twenty-three ATEDH patients with hematomas in temporal area underwent digital subtraction angiography (DSA) detecting bleeding-point. Then, embolization was performed. After embolization, drainage surgery was taken and urokinase was injected into the hematoma cyst by drainage tube to lyse hematoma twice per day.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The results showed that middle meningeal artery was bleeding source. Embolization immediately ceased bleeding. Most clots were resolved and drained after treatment. No recurrence of hematoma or infection was observed.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: The findings suggest that the combined treatments can be an alternative minimally invasive option for ATEDHs, especially for elderly patients or those contraindicated for general anesthesia.
